title: Find the second-highest (and Nth-highest) salary in an employees table — using a subquery and using DENSE_RANK(). (Easy → Medium · Frequently Asked)
hint: Use DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) and filter on rank N, or a subquery selecting MAX(salary) below the overall max.

title: Find the Top-N earners per department using a window function (RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC))
hint: Apply RANK() or DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) in a subquery or CTE and filter rank less than or equal to N.

title: Find employees who are missing a salary value (NULL handling) and identify which employees haven't been paid this cycle
hint: Use WHERE salary IS NULL, since equals NULL never matches; for unpaid this cycle use LEFT JOIN with payments and check IS NULL or NOT EXISTS.

title: Find duplicate records in a table based on a subset of columns
hint: Use GROUP BY on the chosen columns with HAVING COUNT(*) greater than 1 to list the duplicated combinations.

title: Write a self-join query to list each employee alongside their manager's name (employee/manager hierarchy)
hint: Join the employee table to itself, aliasing one as e and one as m on e.manager_id = m.id, using LEFT JOIN to include top-level employees.

title: Write a query computing a running total (cumulative sum) of monthly order amounts using a window function
hint: Group orders by month, then use SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY month) to get the cumulative total.

title: Write a recursive CTE to traverse an org chart or a category tree with unknown depth
hint: Write WITH RECURSIVE with an anchor query for root nodes and a UNION ALL step joining children to the previous level until no rows remain.

title: Given two tables of overlapping products with different prices, write a query returning the minimum price per product across both
hint: UNION ALL the two tables, then GROUP BY product and take MIN(price) for each.

title: Write and explain a query optimization exercise — given a slow query and its EXPLAIN plan, propose an index or rewrite
hint: Read the EXPLAIN plan for full table scans, then add a composite index on filter and join columns, avoid functions on indexed columns, or rewrite subqueries as joins.

title: Given Employee and Department tables, find employees whose salary is greater than their department's average salary. Solve it with a correlated subquery, a JOIN, and a window function
hint: Compute each department's AVG(salary) via a correlated subquery, a join to a grouped derived table, or AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY dept_id), then filter.

title: Delete duplicate rows from a table, keeping only the latest row for each key
hint: Use ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY key ORDER BY updated_at DESC) and delete rows with rn above 1, or a self-join delete keeping the max id.

title: Find employees who earn more than their manager
hint: Self-join employees to their managers on manager_id and filter where the employee's salary exceeds the manager's salary.

title: Find departments that have no employees
hint: LEFT JOIN departments to employees and filter where the employee id IS NULL, or use NOT EXISTS.

title: Find customers who have never placed an order
hint: LEFT JOIN customers to orders and keep rows where order id IS NULL, or use NOT EXISTS; avoid NOT IN with nullable columns.

title: Find the top 3 highest salaries in each department without using LIMIT
hint: Use DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) and filter rank at most 3, or a correlated count of distinct higher salaries below 3.
